choices.ambient_oxygen: o2_pct recorded and o2_basis equal to 'ambient' (the rule of match_environments in pipeline/run.py: any other basis is marked not_ambient); the numbers of counted tests left out because o2_pct is empty and because o2_basis is not 'ambient' are reported per need (excluded_o2_not_recorded, excluded_basis_not_ambient)
choices.counted_tests: need_tests.csv rows with objective_link equal to 'stated'
choices.degenerate_hull: fewer than 3 non-collinear distinct points: hull kind 'point' or 'segment', reported as 'no area'; inside is true only where the nominal point coincides with the point or lies on the segment
choices.flagged_values: a value whose test carries a flag on that axis in the 'flags' column of tests.csv (for example o2_pct:approximate_in_source, o2_pct:range_in_source_start_value_named_in_publication) is used as the number held in tests.csv, like every other value, and is not left out; per need and axis, every counted test with such a flag is listed with its flags and o2_range_as_written, and min, max, nearest and each Pareto test give the number of flagged tests at that value
choices.gap_sign: gap = nearest recorded value minus nominal value; positive means the nearest recorded value is above the nominal value; 0 means a test has exactly the nominal value; where two recorded values are equally near (one above, one below), both are listed
choices.gravity: count of tests whose gravity_level string equals the scenario's gravity_level string; a scenario with gravity_level null sets none; where gravity_level of every test used is a table constant of the team's source mapping, the count equals the number of tests of tables mapped to that level and carries no information beyond that mapping
choices.hull: convex hull of the distinct recorded (o2_pct, pressure_kpa) points, monotone chain, exact rational arithmetic, no tolerance
choices.hull_boundary: a point on an edge or a vertex of the hull is reported as position 'boundary' and counted as inside
choices.nearest_per_axis: the nearest recorded value of each axis is taken over that axis alone; the two axes can have their nearest value in different tests, and neither need be a test of the Pareto set: they are separate answers
choices.no_hull: where no counted test records both values, hull kind is 'none', position is 'no hull' and inside is null (no position is defined)
choices.nominal_rounding: h = half a unit of the last digit written for the nominal value in scenarios.json (70.3 gives 0.05; 21.0 gives 0.05); a gap or Pareto delta with absolute value below h is marked below_nominal_rounding; the 4 corners (nominal +- h on each axis) are placed relative to the hull like the nominal point and the number inside is reported, so a reader sees whether the position changes within the written rounding of the nominal
choices.notes_per_need: every per-need sentence that applies is shown (no_tests where no counted test has ambient oxygen, no_nominal where the scenario has no nominal point); there is no precedence
choices.number_reading: every cell and every spec number is read as the exact decimal it is written as (Python fractions.Fraction of the written string); differences are exact. The cells are the pipeline's standardized values: where a source column has another unit, the pipeline multiplied the cell by a unit factor of pipeline/spec/sources.json and rounded the product to 4 decimals (rule 'number' of pipeline/rules.py); the factor of every source column used is copied under 'conversions'. The nominal values are read as written in scenarios.json and are themselves rounded figures: see 'nominal_rounding'
choices.pareto: a test is listed when no other test of the set has |delta o2_pct| <= its |delta o2_pct| and |delta pressure_kpa| <= its |delta pressure_kpa| with at least one of the two strictly smaller; deltas = test value minus nominal value; no combined distance, no weight, no scaling; tests with identical deltas are all listed; dominance is decided per axis, so a change of unit on either axis does not change the set
choices.pooling: the hull and the Pareto set pool every counted test with ambient oxygen and pressure both recorded, whatever its fuel, flow, geometry or investigation; the tests pooled are reported per investigation_id, fuel_phase and sample_geometry (joint.composition) and in the summary table
choices.ranges: the in_range rule of pipeline/run.py (RANGE_DEFAULTS: min inclusive, max exclusive unless stated) applied to the scenario's ranges; a range the scenario does not set is reported as not set; the joint count requires oxygen and pressure both inside and is asserted equal to tests_atmosphere of scenario_needs.csv
choices.ranges_not_on_axes: a scenario range of a variable that is not one of 'axes' (flow_cms for the ISS) is printed with 'not applied' and enters no count
choices.scenarios_without_nominal: a scenario whose nominal is empty gets no nominal-point numbers; its ranges are reported where set

flex.from: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction

gravity_note: gravity_level in tests.csv is not a column of any PSI table: it is a constant that the team's source mapping (pipeline/spec/sources.json, 'constants') sets for the whole table. The gravity count therefore equals the number of tests of tables the team mapped to the scenario's level and is not a match found in the data.

Every value is the pipeline's standardized value in data/pipeline/tests.csv (with source file and row); where the source unit differs, it is the product of the source cell and the unit factor listed under 'conversions', rounded to 4 decimals by the pipeline. Every other number is a count, minimum, maximum or difference of those values.
These numbers say where tests were run, not what happened in them; no outcome variable is read.

Inside (interior or boundary) means that the nominal point lies in the smallest convex region containing the tested (o2_pct, pressure_kpa) points. It does not mean that a test was run close to it: the deltas of the Pareto table give the distance to the closest tests on each axis. It says nothing about the outcome at this point.
Outside means that the nominal point is not in that region: it lies on the outer side of at least one edge of the hull.
No hull: no counted test of this need records both an ambient oxygen and a pressure, so the nominal point has no position.
The hull and the Pareto set pool all counted tests that record both values, whatever the fuel, geometry, flow or investigation; the summary table names what was pooled.
The nearest value of each axis is taken over that axis alone and can come from a different test on each axis; the Pareto table is a separate answer.

A value flagged in tests.csv (for example 'approximate in source', or the start value of a range written in the source) is used as held; such tests are listed under 'flagged tests' and counted at min, max, nearest and in the Pareto table.
Counts of different needs are not added: one test can be counted for several needs.
scenarios.json gives no nominal point for this environment, so no nominal-point numbers are computed.

gravity_level in tests.csv is not a column of any PSI table: it is a constant that the team's source mapping (pipeline/spec/sources.json, 'constants') sets for the whole table. The gravity count therefore equals the number of tests of tables the team mapped to the scenario's level and is not a match found in the data.
